purpose: Define the separation and explicit causal relationships between Trigger, Event, Runner and Routine in the Core runtime automation surface.

scope: automation dispatch must remain Core/runtime validated

value.name: Trigger to Event to Runner to Routine

metadata.important: This flow is the explicit causality. Topic composition itself does not imply this order.

roles.Trigger: Evaluates a declared condition or trigger surface; it does not itself become Event, Runner or Routine.
roles.Event: Carries an explicitly emitted occurrence/payload; it does not itself execute a Routine.
roles.Runner: Owns bounded execution lifecycle/dispatch context; it is distinct from the Routine definition it may dispatch.
roles.Routine: An inert authored routine definition until explicitly dispatched through the Core runtime.

value.separation_rule: Trigger, Event, Runner and Routine are separate semantic roles even when composed into one automation mechanism.
value.mechanism_rule: The automation mechanism is expressed by composing their Topics and defining only the explicit cross-role causal flow.

value.purpose: Compose Trigger, Event, Runner and Routine Topics into the Core automation mechanism while adding only their explicit cross-role causality.

metadata.composition_rule: Trigger/Event/Runner/Routine semantics remain defined once in their own Topics; this Topic specifies only the automation mechanism connecting them.

invariants.rule: Trigger, Event, Runner and Routine remain distinct semantic roles.
Cross-role execution order exists only where explicitly represented in behavior.flows.

hard_gates.condition: A Trigger is treated as directly executing a Routine without explicit dispatch causality.
Event and Runner semantics are collapsed into one role.
Routine definition executes because it is loaded or read.
Trigger/Event/Runner/Routine Topic composition or visual order is used as execution causality.
Automation dispatch bypasses Core validation or applicable effect authorization.

references.purpose: Uses Core Runtime Automation Topic hierarchy.
Uses Topic composition to reuse Trigger/Event/Runner/Routine semantics.

prose.summary: Composes Trigger, Event, Runner and Routine as a Core automation mechanism while keeping their roles distinct and making the cross-role execution chain explicit flow data.
notes: The contract remains unlocked until referenced source contracts are migrated to 1.4 and their exact identities/operations are reconciled.
Pass 8 formalized previously free Flow actor/data/target/condition/payload/result/error tokens as exact owner-scoped member identities while preserving every source literal.
Pass 9 removed direct operation trace duplication from the composing automation Topic; component operation semantics remain traced through composed Trigger/Event/Runner/Routine Topics.

scope: automation dispatch must remain Core/runtime validated

topics.name: Automation Semantics
topics.purpose: Compose Trigger, Event, Runner and Routine Topics into the Core automation mechanism while adding only their explicit cross-role causality.

metadata.composition_rule: Trigger/Event/Runner/Routine semantics remain defined once in their own Topics; this Topic specifies only the automation mechanism connecting them.

flows.name: Trigger to Event to Runner to Routine

metadata.important: This flow is the explicit causality. Topic composition itself does not imply this order.

roles.Trigger: Evaluates a declared condition or trigger surface; it does not itself become Event, Runner or Routine.
roles.Event: Carries an explicitly emitted occurrence/payload; it does not itself execute a Routine.
roles.Runner: Owns bounded execution lifecycle/dispatch context; it is distinct from the Routine definition it may dispatch.
roles.Routine: An inert authored routine definition until explicitly dispatched through the Core runtime.

semantics.separation_rule: Trigger, Event, Runner and Routine are separate semantic roles even when composed into one automation mechanism.
semantics.mechanism_rule: The automation mechanism is expressed by composing their Topics and defining only the explicit cross-role causal flow.
